title: Local finite rate semi device independent randomness expansion from quantum contextuality
authors: Dhananjoy Ghosh, Nandana J, Jaskaran Singh
abstract: Finite rate randomness expansion (RE) which is secure against quantum adversaries is a crucial information processing task which is well studied in the case of two non-communicating parties sharing Bell non-local correlations in a device independent manner. In this paper we show that contextual correlations with only a single localized party are sufficient for RE in a semi-device independent (SDI) manner. We propose a template SDI-RE protocol which is applicable for arbitrary $N$-cycle non-contextuality (NC) inequalities and derive its RE rate under finite statistics. As a special case, we also highlight the advantages of the situation when RE is constrained by Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt (CHSH) inequality but with characterized measurements implemented by only a single party. Our template protocol also incorporates non-ideal statistics which may not satisfy perfect commutativity and perfect repeatability, both of which are necessary in a loophole-free test of NC inequalities. As such, several recent experimental implementations of significantly loophole-free tests of NC inequalities can be modified for secure RE following our approach.
summary: This paper introduces a template protocol for generating secure quantum randomness (RE) using only contextual correlations measured by a single, localized party. It achieves semi-device independence (SDI) by leveraging violations of N-cycle Non-Contextuality (NC) inequalities. The method is robust as it incorporates quantifiable imperfections in the measurement devices, making it highly relevant for near-term quantum experiments.
main_problem: Developing a secure, finite-rate randomness expansion (RE) protocol that relies only on contextual correlations from a single localized party, rather than requiring multiple non-communicating parties.
main_result: The authors propose a template SDI-RE protocol applicable to arbitrary N-cycle non-contextuality (NC) inequalities, providing a finite-rate security analysis.
method: The protocol involves characterizing measurement device imperfections (repeatability, orthogonality) and using the violation of NC inequalities within a specified confidence interval to extract randomness via a quantum-proof extractor.
model_or_system: The model is based on quantum contextuality, certified by violating N-cycle Non-Contextuality (NC) inequalities, applicable to both odd and even cycle structures.
key_observables: The empirical frequency distribution $	ext{FC}(G)$ relative to the quantum bound $ eta_{	ext{QT}}$ and the total deviation parameter $\delta = \delta_{	ext{stat}} + \delta_{	ext{char}}$.
important_parameters: The number of measurements $N$, the total number of rounds $n$, and the deviation parameters $\epsilon_{rep}, \epsilon_{orth}, \epsilon'_{orth}$.
main_assumptions: The protocol assumes memoryless devices and accounts for non-ideal statistics, including deviations from perfect commutativity and repeatability.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the specific protocols for RE using contextual correlations in odd and even N-cycle scenarios, detailing the measurement and extraction steps.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the need for SDI-RE, then details the template protocol applicable to general N-cycle NC inequalities, providing specific protocols for odd and even N, and finally analyzing the security based on device characterization.
why_interesting: It provides a concrete, experimentally relevant method to generate quantum randomness using only single-party measurements constrained by contextuality, which is a key area in quantum information security.
